analyst_view.overall: Second-bottom Elche (11 points from 13 games, one win in five, 1-1 at Levante on Monday) host third-placed Atletico (31 points, four wins in five, 3-0 at Getafe on Sunday). Atletico play Viking at the Metropolitano in the Champions League on Wednesday, and previews expect Koke and Johnny Cardoso to start on the bench on Saturday, with Pubill back and Lookman and Cuti Romero still out (both now counted by the numbers). Elche coach Martin Anselmi has no suspensions but a long injury list: Lemar (hamstring, counted), Ruben Sanchez (adductor, two to three weeks) and Houary, plus Yago Santiago and Boayar; playmaker Marc Aguado is close to a return from his ankle sprain and may make it. The numbers already count both sides' low recent scoring, and no referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, already trimmed for both sides scoring little lately and now counting Lookman, Romero and Lemar as out. Since my last view Lookman's absence has entered the numbers and Aguado may be back for Elche, while Atletico's changes after Wednesday look limited to midfield, so the earlier small cut no longer holds. I stay at about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, with Atletico's recent low corner count (25 in six) already counted. A Simeone side with a lead tends to sit back and let the home team push, which can bring Elche corners, and Grimaldo's form on the left gives Atletico a source of crosses, but nothing in the news changes the picture. I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already reflecting Elche's 16 cards in their last six and Atletico's quieter run. No referee has been named yet, and a relegation-threatened home side against a top-three team brings intensity the numbers already see. I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots, already lifting Elche (+11%) because Atletico have allowed a lot of shots lately (102 in six). Atletico resting Koke and Cardoso could leave a bit more space, but Elche are short of attackers with Yago Santiago and Boayar out, so the two balance out. I stay at about 26.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already lowering Elche (-6%) for their recent lack of accuracy and Atletico for the absence of Lookman. With Aguado possibly back to feed Elche's attack and Julian Alvarez leading Atletico's line, I no longer see a reason to go below the numbers, so I stay at about 8.3.
